name: PlayStation 5
description: Kyty's own options, then the settings given to Box64 before every PS5 game starts on the phone — KytyPS5 is x86-64 code that Box64 translates. The server runs it natively and ignores the Box64 ones.

sound.label: Sound
sound.description: The session's sound through the phone, or nothing: the emulator still decodes audio, but SDL plays none of it.

occlusionQueries.label: Occlusion queries
occlusionQueries.description: Kyty counts on the GPU what the game asks about hidden objects, so the game skips drawing them. Off, everything counts as visible: more work for the GPU (FF7 Remake at the same spot: 10 frames/s instead of 13.5).

shaderCache.label: Shader cache
shaderCache.description: Kyty keeps the shaders and pipelines each game compiles, and compiles them again from that list when the game starts, before its first frame: a longer start, fewer stutters the first time a scene appears. Kyty's own launcher turns it on.

dynarec.label: Translator (DynaRec)
dynarec.description: Box64 translates the game's x86-64 code into ARM code. Off, it interprets it instead: many times slower, but exact — the way to tell a translation fault from the game's own.

strongMemory.label: Memory ordering
strongMemory.description: How faithfully the translator keeps the x86 memory ordering, which ARM relaxes. Stricter is slower; “Strong” is the usual fix for a multithreaded program that misbehaves.

safeFlags.label: Flags safety
safeFlags.description: How carefully the translator preserves the x86 flags across calls and returns. Box64 ships with 1; KytyPS5 needs 2 on the phone — with 1 the game dies a few seconds after the start (bisected on the S25, 2026-10-14), and 2 costs nothing measurable: every other shortcut can stay on.

bigBlock.label: Block size
bigBlock.description: How much code the translator handles in one block. Smaller blocks are slower but closer to the x86 instruction by instruction.

callRet.label: Call/return optimisation
callRet.description: A shortcut for the x86 call and return instructions. Off is the safest, and on the phone the cheapest: Neptunia ReVerse plays its opening at the same frame rate with a third less processor (66-90 % against 120-145 % with Default, 2026-10-28).

fastNaN.label: Fast NaN
fastNaN.description: Skips the exact propagation of NaN values in floating-point maths. Off is exact and slower.

fastRound.label: Fast rounding
fastRound.description: How the translator rounds floating-point results.

x87Double.label: x87 precision
x87Double.description: The precision of the legacy x87 floating-point unit.

alignedAtomics.label: Aligned atomics
alignedAtomics.description: Treats the x86 atomic operations as aligned. Off is the default.

nativeFlags.label: Native flags
nativeFlags.description: Uses the ARM flags to compute the x86 ones. Off is slower and exact.

selfTest.label: Translator self-test
selfTest.description: Runs every instruction through the interpreter as well and reports the first difference. Extremely slow: diagnostics only.

log.label: Box64 log
log.description: How much Box64 writes to the game's log.
